transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-09
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Meeting ID: ff-20271109-pol-01
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Singh (Redwood); Aisha Khan, Tom Reynolds, Laura Park, Evan Ortiz (Polaris)

Summary:
- Renewal discussion for Polaris account (current term ends Dec 31, 2027).
- Polaris is interested in expanding Dedicated capacity and adding APAC region for lower latency for their Singapore storefronts.
- Procurement and legal want a two-step: pricing and SOC2/network docs, then PO + signature.

Topics:
- Current usage and pain points (burst limits, cold-start latency)
- Dedicated capacity sizing and autoscale policies
- APAC region deployment options (hosted vs private VPC)
- Contract term and pricing for renewal + expansion
- Next steps: quote, benchmark, security docs

Action items (recapped in call):
- Redwood to send revised quote for 18-month renewal + APAC add-on
- SE to run benchmark plan with Polaris infra team
- CS to share onboarding docs and success metrics

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Maya, your AE. Diego is our solutions engineer, Priya is your CSM.
[00:08] Aisha Khan: Hi all, Aisha here. we want to make sure we cover capacity & the APAC region today.
[00:13] Tom Reynolds: yeah, and procurement's on the call for timeline stuff. Laura, Evan are here too.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great. quick context: your current hosted plan runs, what did we say, about 120M tokens/month and a Dedicated pool sized at 4xA10G equivalent on peak, correct?
[00:30] Evan Ortiz: yep roughly, although our peak patterns have spiky hours during SE Asia morning which is causing tail latency.
[00:38] Diego Alvarez: Right, so the tail's likely due to cross-region hops and cold kv cache misses when requests route back to NA. if we add an APAC region with a local cache, that should cut median latency in half.
[00:51] Aisha Khan: Can you clarify cache — you mean the KV cache? sometimes our folks write K V cache in docs, gets confusing.
[00:58] Diego Alvarez: yeah KV cache — key value. Redwood's runtime supports prefix caching and also a warm pool to reduce cold starts.
[01:06] Tom Reynolds: What's the uplift on cost if we add APAC region hosted vs Dedicated in APAC?
[01:12] Maya Chen: good question. hosted APAC add-on is basically a regional bandwidth and infra surcharge — small for steady traffic but spikes can add cost. Dedicated in APAC gives predictable throughput — you pay reserved monthly for the pool but unit cost per token is lower during high volume.
[01:28] Laura Park: From procurement side we prefer predictable monthly commit and a fixed unit price, makes budgeting easier.
[01:33] Priya Singh: noted. for customers moving to Dedicated we usually work through a capacity plan — Diego, want to walk through recommended sizing?
[01:40] Diego Alvarez: sure. Based on current peaks, I recommend bumping to a 6x pool and enabling burst capacity at 8x for holiday spikes; that covers 99.5th percentile without routing to NA. Also enable prefix caching for common storefront prompts.
[01:55] Evan Ortiz: curious about autoscale — our infra team relies on predictable autoscale windows, can Redwood's autoscale integrate with our policies?
[02:02] Diego Alvarez: yes, autoscale can be policy-driven; you can set min/max, cooldowns, and also a cost cap trigger to avoid runaway spend. integrations via API and alert hooks.
[02:12] Aisha Khan: Security question — we need SOC 2, SSO, and KMS integration. we also have a requirement for audit logs retention for 7 years.
[02:20] Maya Chen: we have SOC 2 Type II — we'll share the report. SSO via SAML/Okta is supported, RBAC is available, and KMS/HSM integrations for key management. audit logs are available in the Console, retention is an add-on but we can include longer retention in enterprise package.
[02:36] Tom Reynolds: any gotchas for private VPC vs hosted APAC?
[02:40] Diego Alvarez: Private VPC gives you customer-managed network and is required if you need air-gapped or stricter egress controls; it's more setup and OPEX vs hosted but gives full network control. Hosted APAC is faster to set up.
[02:51] Laura Park: timeline wise, procurement needs a quote and security docs to start legal. can we get a proposal by next Friday?
[02:57] Maya Chen: yes we can target Nov 12. we'll include a few options — 12-month renewal, 18-month with discount, and dedicated APAC add-on pricing.
[03:07] Aisha Khan: on the technical side we want to run a benchmark — 99th percentile latency expectations and throughput tests. Evan can coordinate.
[03:14] Evan Ortiz: I'll need Diego's test plan and the scripts to run against our staging, prefer week of Nov 15.
[03:20] Diego Alvarez: I'll prepare a benchmark plan — CPU/GPU trace, load profile, warm vs cold cache runs, and instructions for the KV cache warmup.
[03:29] Tom Reynolds: Is there any migration downtime for moving to Dedicated in APAC?
[03:33] Priya Singh: minimal, we typically do canary traffic shifting and automatic fallback. Diego, correct?
[03:38] Diego Alvarez: yes canary + A/B routing. no planned downtime; you'll route a percentage of traffic for validation then shift.
[03:44] Aisha Khan: Are there model compatibility constraints across regions? we use a quantized Llama variant for cheaper ops.
[03:51] Diego Alvarez: models are portable; runtime picks kernels appropriate to the hardware. for quantized variants we validate performance — sometimes kernel availability differs by GPU type but we maintain parity for supported combos.
[04:03] Laura Park: on contracts, procurement asked about early termination clauses and renewal escalation. can we do an 18-month term with a 60-day termination notice and a capped price increase?
[04:12] Maya Chen: we can propose an 18-month commitment with a limited escalation clause. legal will need to confirm but it's a common request.
[04:20] Tom Reynolds: also curious about traffic encryption end-to-end and if traffic between APAC region and NA model store is encrypted.
[04:26] Diego Alvarez: yes TLS for all control and data plane traffic, and cross-region sync uses encrypted channels. if you use Private deployment we can support dedicated interconnects.
[04:35] Aisha Khan: any competitive points we should highlight vs Anthropic or Bedrock?
[04:39] Maya Chen: Redwood's emphasis is production-first: predictable latency controls, cost-aware batching, and a unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. vs Bedrock you get more opinionated inference controls; vs self-hosted Triton you get less ops burden.
[04:52] Evan Ortiz: good — costs are critical. do you have an estimate of unit token price at 6x pool dedicated?
[04:58] Maya Chen: I'll include precise numbers in the quote but expect 15-25% lower unit cost versus hosted at scale, plus lower variability.
[05:06] Tom Reynolds: one more question — compliance: we need an audit trail export for e-discovery. is that available?
[05:12] Priya Singh: yes audit exports and event logs can be exported and integrated with SIEMs.
[05:16] Aisha Khan: ok, that covers high level. let's go into the benchmark specifics — Diego?
[05:20] Diego Alvarez: benchmark plan: we'll run three phases: baseline (your current NA-hosted routing), APAC-hosted (new region but hosted), and Dedicated-APAC. each with warm and cold runs. we'll measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost per second. I'll send the script and measurement templates.
[05:37] Evan Ortiz: sounds good. will you need service account keys for the staging?
[05:40] Diego Alvarez: yes we'll need a staging service account with limited scope; Evan can provision.
[05:45] Laura Park: procurement will also need the contract redlines — prefer to see them before PO.
[05:49] Maya Chen: understood, we'll share a proposed MSA and SLAs.
[05:53] Aisha Khan: anything else on monitoring? we want per-route latency dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns.
[05:58] Priya Singh: that's in Console — per-route/model dashboards, and we can enable detailed retention for a fee.
[06:05] Tom Reynolds: ok let's recap next steps.
[06:08] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood sends revised quote by Nov 12; Diego sends benchmark plan by Nov 11; Evan and Diego to run staging tests week of Nov 15; Redwood shares SOC2 and network diagram by Nov 12; Polaris confirms procurement timeline by Nov 30.
[06:28] Laura Park: confirmed.
[06:30] Aisha Khan: thank you, looking forward to the benchmark.
[06:33] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[06:36] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attributions and small recognition errors (e.g., "K V cache" vs "KV cache"). Some product names may be slightly off in auto transcript (Redwood Dedicated sometimes appears as "Redwood dedicate"), but content preserved.
